sections.title: The Call of Jeremiah
observations: Jeremiah's call to be a prophet is significant as it emphasizes God's sovereignty in choosing His messengers. God knew Jeremiah even before he was formed in the womb, indicating a divine purpose and plan for his life from the very beginning.
The phrase 'I appointed you a prophet to the nations' highlights the universal scope of Jeremiah's mission, not just limited to Israel but extending to all nations.

sections.title: Jeremiah's Hesitation and God's Assurance
observations: Jeremiah expresses his youth and inexperience as a reason for his reluctance to speak. This reflects a common theme in scripture where God calls individuals who feel inadequate for the task.

God reassures Jeremiah by touching his mouth and putting His words in Jeremiah's mouth, symbolizing divine empowerment and authority. This act signifies that the message is not Jeremiah's own but God's.

importantVerses.commentary: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But the Lord said to me, 'Do not say, I am only a youth; for to all to whom I send you, you shall go, and whatever I command you, you shall speak.'

questions: What does Jeremiah's call reveal about God's knowledge and purpose for individuals?
How does God's reassurance to Jeremiah apply to our own feelings of inadequacy when called to serve?
In what ways can we discern God's calling in our own lives today?
